served.stem: A person drinks alcohol, which inhibits the release of antidiuretic hormone. What is the expected result?
choices: Less glucose reabsorption in the proximal tubule
A higher filtration rate at the glomerulus with no change in urine concentration
More aquaporins in the collecting duct, so less urine is produced
Fewer aquaporins in the collecting duct, so more dilute urine is produced
More Na+ reabsorption in the distal tubule, so blood pressure rises
served.bankWhy: ADH is the water saver. It puts aquaporin water channels into the collecting duct so water can leave the filtrate and return to the blood. Take ADH away and the water stays in the tubule, so urine is plentiful and dilute.

answer.text: Fewer aquaporins in the collecting duct, so more dilute urine is produced
answer.line: ADH puts water channels into the collecting duct. Less ADH means fewer channels, so water stays in the urine.

steps: Name the hormone's job. ADH, the water saver, inserts aquaporins into the collecting duct.
Alcohol blocks its release, so fewer channels go in. Water stays in the tubule.
Result: more urine, and more dilute.

choices.text: Less glucose reabsorption in the proximal tubule
choices.note: Glucose spills into urine when blood glucose overwhelms the proximal transporters, as in diabetes mellitus. ADH does not handle glucose.

choices.text: A higher filtration rate at the glomerulus with no change in urine concentration
choices.note: Filtration is a nearby step that ADH does not set. And urine concentration is exactly what changes.

choices.text: More aquaporins in the collecting duct, so less urine is produced
choices.note: That is ADH at work. Blocking its release runs the other way.

choices.text: Fewer aquaporins in the collecting duct, so more dilute urine is produced
choices.note: No ADH, fewer water channels: the water leaves in the urine.

choices.text: More Na+ reabsorption in the distal tubule, so blood pressure rises
choices.note: Sodium reabsorption in the distal nephron is the effect of aldosterone, the neighboring hormone, not ADH.

student.lockIt: ADH saves water by adding aquaporins. Less ADH: more urine, and more dilute.
